characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever controls the technical risk vs. scope trade-off by demonstrating the feasibility of platform-neutral and fallback-capable authentication methods. Its objectives are to create credible technical evidence that secure, standards-based access models are feasible without exclusive reliance on Apple or Google as trust anchors. Key success metrics include the development of working non-production demonstrators (one mobile-oriented, one browser-based or hardware-token-based fallback) and securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority to the project's proposal.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever ID: 80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it provides concrete evidence to support policy proposals, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy (lever ID: f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) as it informs procurement decisions with credible technical demonstrations.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Coalition Building Strategy (lever ID: 1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as a narrow focus on technical feasibility might limit coalition building efforts, and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever ID: 2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as it may not fully align with broader European standards requirements.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy lever controls the political risk vs. coalition size trade-off by reframing issues in terms of resilience, continuity of service, procurement neutrality, and supplier concentration risk. Its objectives are to influence AltID requirements and increase adoption of platform-neutral standards. Key success metrics include submitting policy proposals and securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever ID: bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it provides concrete evidence to support policy proposals, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy (lever ID: f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) as it informs procurement decisions with credible policy backing.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Coalition Building Strategy (lever ID: 1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as a narrow focus on policy advocacy might limit coalition building efforts, and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever ID: 2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as it may not fully align with broader European standards requirements.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy lever controls the speed vs. breadth of support trade-off by building a coalition spanning security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers. Its objectives are to amplify advocacy efforts and increase political pressure for platform neutrality. Key success metrics include stakeholder engagement increased and securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever ID: 80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it provides a broad coalition to support policy proposals, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy (lever ID: f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) as it informs procurement decisions with credible coalition backing.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever ID: bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as a narrow focus on coalition building might limit technical feasibility efforts, and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever ID: 2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as it may not fully align with broader European standards requirements.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy lever controls the specificity vs. implementability trade-off by advocating for platform-neutral language and certified fallback authentication paths in AltID procurement documents. Its objectives are to drive adoption of platform-neutral access models and reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Key success metrics include securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority and including platform-neutral language in procurement documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever ID: bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it informs procurement decisions with credible technical demonstrations, and with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever ID: 80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it provides policy backing for platform-neutral language.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Coalition Building Strategy (lever ID: 1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as a narrow focus on procurement influence might limit coalition building efforts, and with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (lever ID: 2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) as it may not fully align with broader European standards requirements.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy lever controls the resource allocation vs. scope of influence trade-off by engaging with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups to advocate for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards. Its objectives are to create broader impact, increase interoperability, and reduce lock-in across Europe. Key success metrics include input provided to relevant EU bodies and securing a formal written response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or another relevant authority.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (lever ID: bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it provides technical evidence to support EU standards requirements, and with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (lever ID: 80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as it informs policy proposals with credible EU backing.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Coalition Building Strategy (lever ID: 1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as a narrow focus on EU standards engagement might limit coalition building efforts, and with the Procurement Influence Strategy (lever ID: f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) as it may not fully align with broader European procurement requirements.
